description: Role catalog for the seeded fleet. A scenario names a fixture ROLE; the runner (hack/fleet-kubeconfigs.sh) discovers the leased project's seeded clusters by label, matches each to a slot below, confirms every object in the role's `probes` list is present, and only then writes that role's kubeconfig. A project-scoped role (`cluster_slot: null`: a Compute Engine object no cluster carries) is probed in the project with gcloud and published as `<role>.confirmed` alone, with no kubeconfig. Nothing outside this file may address a seeded cluster or an eval project directly: each project carries its own set, so a case written against one must run unchanged against all of them. Names, prefix and location are deliberately absent -- they are the Terraform's business and are read back off the discovered clusters. See README.md, 'Addressing a fixture by role'. One sanctioned exception, which discovers by these same labels and the trailing -<slot> name rule: hack/ci-eval-pr.sh section 3b reuses the slot-c cluster as the gpu-stress-test log-fixture subject -- it mutates nothing in-cluster, writes only project-level Cloud Logging entries that name the cluster, and falls back to a per-run cluster when slot c is absent, not RUNNING, or its default namespace is not empty. hack/fleet-fixture-state.py discovers nothing: it reads the slot's cluster name and location back out of the `.fleet-context` file the runner wrote, for the `cluster` state subjects below. kube_agents_bench.scope_exclude reads the same file, for a case that declares `scope_exclude:`, to name a slot's cluster in the install's spec.scope.exclude.clusters for that case's repetitions; it discovers nothing either.
probe_syntax: Each probe is `<kind>/<name>` or `<kind>?<label-selector>`, read against the role's `namespace` when it has one. A project-scoped role (`cluster_slot: null`, for a Compute Engine object no cluster carries) takes `<kind>/<name-prefix>*` instead, where the kind is `instance` or `firewall`: the runner lists the project's instances or firewall rules whose name starts with the prefix, with gcloud, and the probe passes when at least one is there. The prefix stops before the fleet's `cluster_prefix`, which is the Terraform's business. A role's namespace is probed implicitly. A probe is the runner's promise that the object was THERE before the agent ran, and it is the only thing that entitles a check to call the same object's later absence a violation rather than an environment that was never ready -- so every subject a task.yaml asserts on must appear here, which bench/tests/test_fleet_verifier.py enforces in both directions. A role with an empty list confirms nothing, and its checks can never blame the run for an absence.
state_syntax: Presence is not state (#1278: every probe passed while payments-api sat Pending on 30 projects). Each `state` entry is one assertion about the DESIGNED observable state of a role whose probes passed, evaluated by hack/fleet-fixture-state.py after the runner publishes the role: `subject` is a probe-shaped `<kind>/<name>`, on a project-scoped role a probe-shaped `<kind>/<name-prefix>*` (every Compute Engine object of that kind whose name starts with the prefix, read with `gcloud compute ... list --format json`), `<kind>?<label-selector>` or bare `<kind>?` (every object of that kind in the role's namespace), or the word `cluster` for the GKE cluster carrying the role, read with `clusters describe` on the name the runner recorded; `path` is a dotted field path with `[*]`, `[N]`, `[?(@.key=='value')]` or `["quoted.key"]` steps, the last for a label or selector key the bare form cannot carry (`metadata.labels["pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce-version"]`); `op` is `eq`, `ge`, `any_eq`, `any_ge`, `none_eq` (each with a `value`), `absent` (no value, no objects or no values at the path), `after_now` (an RFC 3339 timestamp still ahead), `age_hours_ge` (an RFC 3339 timestamp at least `value` hours in the past; an unparseable one fails), `minor_behind_channel_default` (cluster subject only: the minor is `value` behind the cluster's own release channel default), `not_ahead_of_channel` (cluster subject only, no value: the version is in the cluster's own release channel's `validVersions` in get-server-config, or that list has a newer patch of the same minor, or a newer version when it carries none of that minor; an unrecognised version string fails), or `node_cpu_spare_ge` (a `node?<selector>` subject with no path: at least one node matches and every matched node keeps at least `value` millicores of allocatable CPU unrequested by the pods bound to it, counted the way the scheduler counts a pod, the larger of its containers' sum with restartable init containers and its biggest ordinary init container, plus pod overhead, Succeeded and Failed pods excluded; a matched node not yet reporting allocatable leaves the role not checked); `why` says what the cases lose when it fails. A role whose fixture is present but fails any assertion is DRIFTED: scripts/verify_ci_pool_project.py fails the project, and the script writes `<role>.drift` beside the role's kubeconfig, one failed assertion per line with what was observed (#1544). The presubmit does not run this pass and never acts on a drift; a scheduled scan of every pool project from the CI health bot is the follow-up on #1550. A role with an empty list asserts nothing beyond presence. A `value` may be an object or an empty object; it is compared whole and structurally (key order does not matter), so an `emptyDir` with no fields is `{}`. One key of a label or selector map is asserted through the quoted step, not by comparing the whole map, so a key another owner adds is not drift.

cluster_slots.a: The seeded workload namespaces (each role's `namespace` names its own), plus the idle and pinned node pools, the default pool's own headroom, and the GKE Config Connector add-on in namespaced mode, the cluster the Config Connector eval cases plant on. Labelled `upgrade-family=seeded-regular`, the rollout family it shares with slots c and d.
cluster_slots.b: Control plane held one minor behind the REGULAR channel default, plus the upgrade-readiness drain defects. Labelled `upgrade-family=seeded-held`: a rollout family of its own, so the regular family's rollout never waits on the lag.
cluster_slots.c: The consistency outlier: no master authorized networks, and a default pool on a 50 GB boot disk with cpuCfsQuota off where every other pool runs 20 GB and no kubelet block. Also the ComputeClass cluster (defects-c.tf), the one whose only pool carries a compute-class label: ComputeClass `general-ccc` over the labelled, untainted default pool, the namespace `seeded-compute-class` with three small running workloads, NodeLocal DNSCache off, and no NetworkPolicy anywhere, because two nightly cases read this slot as the cluster with none. Labelled `upgrade-family=seeded-regular`.
cluster_slots.d: Multi-zonal: nodes in two zones, carrying the zonal-skew fixtures. The only slot whose shape is the fixture. Labelled `upgrade-family=seeded-regular`.

state.subject: cronjob/legacy-endpoints-writer

state.subject: cronjob/legacy-endpoints-writer

state.subject: job?app=legacy-endpoints-writer

The condition, not the pod counter: a Job whose pod was never admitted fails with the counter absent, and one whose pod was replaced mid-run fails with it at 2. ttlSecondsAfterFinished 900 clears a transient in fifteen minutes; a failure that persists is the fixture, not the weather
